claims.text: The Kesik Minare, or Broken Minaret Mosque, has one of the most layered histories of any building in Turkey, originally built as a Roman temple in the 2nd century AD.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: In the 7th century it was converted into a Byzantine church dedicated to the Virgin Mary, though it was heavily damaged during the Arab invasions of that same century.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The minaret was added in the early 13th century when the Sultanate of Rum established their rule in Antalya and converted the church into a mosque.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: In 1361, when the crusader king of Cyprus captured Antalya from the Seljuks, it was consecrated as a church again, only to become a mosque once more under Ottoman rule.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The main building was tragically destroyed in a fire in 1896, leaving only the surviving minaret standing on Hesapçı Street.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: After restoration work beginning in 2018 and the top cone being restored in 2019, the structure officially reopened as a mosque in 2021, welcoming worshippers for the first time in nearly 125 years.
claims.subject: self
